predecessors.name: Sumerian city-states
predecessors.text: Sumer, Lugal-zage-si's kingdom, 'around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292'

predecessors.name: Mari
predecessors.text: Mari and the middle Euphrates, destroyed by Sargon c.

predecessors.name: Ebla
predecessors.text: 'the Upper Land: Mari, Iarmuti, and Ebla'

successors.name: Gutian dynasty
successors.text: 'northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish', the last Akkadian kingdom under Dudu and Shu-turul

successors.name: Second Dynasty of Lagash
successors.text: Lagash, Girsu and Nina, independent under Ur-Baba from c.

successors.name: Elam
successors.text: Susiana, a vassal 'since the time of Sargon' until Elam 'claim[ed] independence' under Shar-kali-sharri

ledger.x: 2334 BCE: Sargon founds the kingdom of Akkad.
2300 BCE: Ebla's first kingdom falls; Sargon claims the Upper Land.
2290 BCE: Susa and Warahshe become Akkad's vassals.
2279 BCE: Rimush faces a Sumerian revolt.
2254 BCE: the Great Revolt against Naram-Sin.
2253 BCE: Naram-Sin crushes the Great Revolt.
2189 BCE: Akkad shrinks to Akkad and Kish.
2164 BCE: Lagash is independent under Ur-Baba.

wars.name: Sargon's conquests
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Conquests of Sargon of Akkad: c.

wars.name: Rimush's campaigns
wars.outcome: The revolt of Kaku of Ur crushed with 'heavy casualties in Sumer'; campaigns 'against Elam, Awan, and Marhashi' (Emahsini defeated, Awan page).

wars.name: Manishtushu's campaigns
wars.outcome: 'campaigned against Anshan and Sherihum on the Iranian Plateau and claimed to have subjugated Magan after sending ships across the Persian Gulf'; Mari restored under a Shakkanakku (c.

wars.name: Great Revolt against Naram-Sin
wars.outcome: Suppressed; Naram-Sin's reign went on to its peak.

wars.name: Naram-Sin's campaigns
wars.outcome: 'His campaigns reached Upper Mesopotamia and northern Syria' (stele at Pir Hüseyin near Diyarbakır); Armanum and Ebla claimed; Magan 'said to have' been subjugated; a treaty with Awan (Khita or Helu).

wars.name: Gutian war and the fall of Akkad
wars.outcome: 'The Gutians raided Mesopotamia in the final decades, and some settled near Adab'; Akkad shrank to 'northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish' and ended c.

certainty.note: No surveyed line: the Sumerian core follows the city territories, the Upper Land, Elamite and Gulf claims are campaign reaches; the Diyala and Zagros edge is a march.
